trust_decision.summary: Whether an outbound HTTPS notification that carries a Bitbucket Server HTTP-access (Bearer) token validates the peer certificate chain and hostname. Decided in BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.send, which hands the Apache HttpClient a trust-all SSLContext (TrustStrategy returns true for every cert) plus NoopHostnameVerifier; the published fix replaces that client with HttpClients.createSystem().

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is exactly 'unconditionally disables SSL/TLS certificate validation'; the only trust-all TrustStrategy and the only NoopHostnameVerifier in the tree are these four lines, so grepping for either lands here.

fix_sites.entry_point: BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.send(StringCredentials, Verb, String, String) (public API), reached through BitBucketPPRServerClient.send(String,String) for build status and BitBucketPPRServerClient.send(Verb,...) for approve/decline
same Bearer send, POST branch (unrelated blank-payload cleanup folded into this commit: the unconditional duplicate setEntity is removed)

BitBucketPPRClientServerVisitor.send(StandardCredentials, String, String) / send(StandardCredentials, Verb, ...) StringCredentials branch, reached from BitBucketPPRClientFactory.createClient(SERVER, ...) in BitBucketPPRHandlerTemplate.callClient
same visitor, private send(StringCredentials, ...) delegating to BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.send

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Trust material must keep coming from the Jenkins JVM's configured JSSE trust store, and JVM proxy settings (https.proxyHost and friends) must keep working: a Bitbucket Server fronted by a private CA or a self-signed certificate has to be made to work by adding that CA to the trust store (the fix's own comment says so), and Jenkins controllers commonly reach hosts through a system proxy. An over-broad fix that hard-codes or pins a trust anchor, only accepts public CAs, or uses HttpClients.createDefault()/custom() without system properties breaks those deployments silently.

O6_input_shapes: Verb.POST with a non-blank JSON payload (post-fix the entity is set only inside the isNotBlank guard, fix.diff:110-115)
Verb.POST with a blank payload, which the pinned code sends as an empty application/json entity (BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.java:83-86) and the fix sends with no entity
Verb.DELETE with no payload for pull-request approve/decline (BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.java:90-95)
Destination URL may be http or https: the pinned registry registers both schemes (BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.java:67-69), and the URL is a clone href or an admin propagationUrl

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A persisted admin option such as trustSelfSignedCertificates or a customTrustStore path whose empty/default value builds a trust-all SSLContext for the notification client
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The trust-all existed precisely to serve self-signed/private-CA Bitbucket Server installs, and the fix's comment tells those operators to configure the JVM trust store instead, so a maintainer would plausibly put that switch in GlobalConfiguration; the defaults path is never visited by a TLS check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second client construction in the same package that also gets a hand-built SSLConnectionSocketFactory with a no-op verifier
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: There are three parallel consumers (BasicAuth, OAuth2, Bearer), each building its own HTTP client; a maintainer applying 'the same custom SSL setup' to all of them for consistency is a natural edit, and BasicAuth currently only validates because it happens to use HttpClientBuilder.create().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A destination guard (https-only, or host must match the SCM URL) placed next to URL construction in the action/handler layer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The notification URL is assembled here from the webhook payload or the propagationUrl, so a maintainer fixing 'the token goes somewhere unexpected' could add the check here and cover only this action, missing the push observer and the DELETE links.

O9_family: improper certificate validation (CWE-295): TLS peer certificate chain and hostname are not verified before an access token is sent

O10_build.toolchain: Maven wrapper (mvnw) with the Jenkins plugin parent 5.0 building an HPI; jenkins.version 2.479.3 (pom.xml:19-20), maven-hpi-plugin 3.57 (pom.xml:241-244), surefire 2.22.2 (pom.xml:251-254); CI on JDK 21 and 17 (Jenkinsfile:8-11); JUnit 5 + Mockito; scribejava-core 8.3.3 (pom.xml:128-130)
O10_build.project_tests: src/test/java/io/jenkins/plugins/bitbucketpushandpullrequest/client/api/BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumerTest.java:36-55 is the only client/HTTP test and is a @Disabled no-op at the pinned commit; the fix rewrites it into sendRejectsUntrustedCertificate, which starts a local com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpsServer with a keytool-generated self-signed cert. Webhook-receiver, action and filter tests exist but none touch TLS.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the trust-all TrustStrategy with HttpClients.createDefault() or a bare SSLContexts.createSystemDefault() socket factory while keeping NoopHostnameVerifier or the custom BasicHttpClientConnectionManager: the self-signed-certificate test still throws, so the fix looks validated, but hostname verification stays off and JVM system-proxy settings are still ignored.

out_of_scope_notes: Notification destinations are data-driven: the server action takes the base URL from the webhook payload's links.clone[].href (action/BitBucketPPRPullRequestServerAction.java:90-95, action/BitBucketPPRServerRepositoryAction.java:76-81) or from the admin-set propagationUrl (config/BitBucketPPRPluginConfig.java:98-103), and the receiving hook is an UnprotectedRootAction (receiver/BitBucketPPRHookReceiver.java:71), so a crafted webhook can direct a stored Bearer token to an arbitrary host; that is destination injection/SSRF-class, not certificate validation, so it was not pursued.

propagationUrl is validated only for URL syntax (config/BitBucketPPRPluginConfig.java:106-118), so an http:// destination would carry the Bearer token in cleartext - CWE-319, outside this advisory's certificate-validation property.
The same commit also removes an unconditional duplicate setEntity() in the Bearer consumer (fix.diff:110-115; pinned consumer:83-86), a payload-handling bug unrelated to TLS.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell/du in this session); the tree is ~193 Java sources plus docs and images, which looks well under 5 MB, but tiny_repo was left unflagged for lack of a measurement.

The Bitbucket Cloud OAuth2 route (client/api/BitBucketPPROAuth2ApiConsumer.java:44-58) delegates TLS to scribejava-core 8.3.3, whose source is not vendored in this tree; I relied on the library default (JVM trust store + default hostname verifier), so its validation is asserted from library defaults, not from a file:line here.
No later tree or release is available for this repo ('latest release: none'), so O8 present_in_latest is unknown and latest_where is empty.

The pinned tree already contains the same test class with a @Disabled no-op testSend (src/test/java/io/jenkins/plugins/bitbucketpushandpullrequest/client/api/BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumerTest.java:36-55); the added sendRejectsUntrustedCertificate test is not present, so regression_tests_in_pinned_commit was not flagged.

single_site is flagged on the basis that the security change is the one client construction in BearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.send; the diff literally touches three methods in two files, but the other two hunks are exception-signature cleanup that is not needed to compile or to pass the certificate test.

SSLException extends IOException, which BitBucketPPRClientServerVisitor catches and only logs (client/BitBucketPPRClientServerVisitor.java:64-66,73-75), so a test routed through the public visitor would not observe the rejection; the published test calls the consumer directly, and the hidden tests are assumed to do the same.
